blocks.text: Rubber molding is a manufacturing process used to produce custom components from natural or synthetic elastomer materials.

During the molding process, uncured rubber is formed within a precision mold using heat and pressure. For most conventional thermoset rubber compounds, a chemical curing process known as vulcanization creates cross-links within the material, producing an elastic component with its intended mechanical and physical properties.
The finished rubber component can be engineered to provide sealing, flexibility, vibration isolation, chemical resistance, abrasion resistance, and other characteristics required for its application.
Rubber molding is commonly used to manufacture components that must maintain reliable performance under mechanical loads, repeated movement, environmental exposure, or demanding operating conditions.

blocks.text: SYNC offers complementary rubber molding processes to support a wide range of applications, materials, and production requirements.
Compression molding is one of the most widely used processes for manufacturing custom rubber components.
A measured amount of uncured rubber is placed directly into a heated mold cavity. Pressure is applied as the mold closes, allowing the material to flow and cure into the intended geometry.
Compression molding is particularly useful for larger components, thick-section parts, relatively straightforward geometries, and applications where tooling economics are important.
Transfer molding introduces uncured rubber into a heated chamber, where pressure forces it into a closed mold cavity.
This process can provide advantages for components with intricate features, metal inserts, and specialized bonding requirements.
Typical applications include rubber-to-metal assemblies, seals, bushings, electrical components, and precision industrial parts.
Rubber injection molding uses specialized equipment to introduce prepared elastomer material into a heated mold, where it cures into the finished component.
Depending on material and tooling requirements, the process can offer advantages in repeatability, material control, and production efficiency.
Injection molding may be particularly effective for recurring production programs involving complex molded components.

items.title: Butyl Rubber (IIR)

a: Custom rubber molding is a manufacturing process that forms natural or synthetic elastomers into components designed for specific applications. Typical products include seals, gaskets, bushings, mounts, valve components, and bonded assemblies.

items.q: What rubber molding processes does SYNC offer?
a: SYNC's rubber molding capabilities include compression molding, transfer molding, and specialized rubber injection molding, along with silicone processing and rubber-to-metal bonding.
The preferred process depends on component design, material requirements, tooling, and expected production volume.

items.q: What rubber materials can SYNC mold?
a: Common materials include EPDM, nitrile, silicone, neoprene, natural rubber, SBR, FKM, HNBR, butyl rubber, and specialty elastomers.

items.q: Can SYNC develop custom rubber compounds?
a: Yes. SYNC has in-house rubber compounding expertise and material development resources to support applications requiring specialized physical, mechanical, or environmental properties.

items.q: Can rubber be molded directly onto metal?
a: Yes. Rubber-to-metal bonding can integrate rubber with prepared metal substrates to produce functional assemblies such as mounts, valve components, bushings, and industrial rollers.

items.q: Does SYNC manufacture large rubber parts?
a: Yes. Our manufacturing resources support large-format compression molding for specialized industrial rubber components. Maximum dimensions depend on tooling, material, and equipment requirements.

items.q: Can SYNC help with an existing rubber part or tooling transfer?
a: Yes. Our teams can evaluate existing drawings, tooling, material specifications, and production requirements to determine an appropriate manufacturing approach.

items.q: What information is needed for a rubber molding quote?
a: A drawing or 3D model, material specifications, estimated annual volume, application requirements, and any existing tooling information are helpful.
Our engineering team can assist if the material or molding process has not yet been determined.
